report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a modest, specific difference — Model B increases probability/magnitude of sensational, tabloid-y and coarse/offensive tokens (and some headline/section-style tokens) relative to Model A, especially at the start of continuations.

Why I think this
- Repeated top logit-lens tokens are strongly suggestive: high-ranked tokens include TMZ, cannibal, scammers, freak, scammers, scammers, kicking words like hated/deadly/destruction/graves, and coarse/offensive tokens such as fucking, herpes, homosexual, immigrant (in contexts that can be pejorative). Many other top tokens are tabloidy or sensational proper-nouns (TMZ, DJI, Playboy) or short intensifiers/colloquialisms (Basically, genuinely, freak, terrifying).
- The L2-norm pattern shows the difference concentrated early in the sequence (pos0 is very large across many layers) and then also in the mid-to-late layers (layers ~16–25). That pattern is consistent with a change that affects the model’s initial token choices and the later-stage selection of high-level lexical/content tokens (i.e., affects what kind of headline/label/style the model starts with and then reinforces it in later layers).
- Some tokens like Summary, Outcome, Waiter, plaintext, and astrolog appear in later positions’ top directions, suggesting the change also nudges the model toward more explicit section-heading / short-label style continuations in addition to sensational content.

Caveats / uncertainty
- The patchscope readouts were not shown, so I can’t verify how this vector changes full-sentence continuations; the logit-lens evidence is token-level and limited to tokens seen >=5 times.
- The signal could reflect a mixture of topics (tabloid/gossip + violent/negative vocabulary + some offensive terms) rather than a single narrow “toxic” objective. I therefore describe the difference at the level the evidence supports: an increased propensity for sensational/tabloid and coarse/offensive lexical choices, especially at the start of generated continuations.

If you want, I can (a) try to reconstruct likely continuations by applying the difference vector to prompts, or (b) produce a shorter list of the most diagnostic tokens and layers to inspect further.
